verdict: Emerson closed its fiscal year with sales up 7% to $5.2B and profit up sharply — pre-tax margin widened to 19.2% — as every business group grew and long-cycle project demand stayed strong.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Net sales of $5.20B, vs $4.86B a year ago; underlying sales (excluding currency and deals) rose 4%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.07 a year ago, up 24%; adjusted EPS was $1.86

kpis.label: Adjusted segment EBITA
kpis.note: Profit of the business segments before interest, tax and amortization — a 29.1% margin, up from 27.5%

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash from operations of $1,075M less capital spending — up 9% from a year ago

segments.name: Final Control
segments.note: Valves, actuators and regulators that control the flow of liquids and gases in industrial plants — the largest single business.

segments.name: Control Systems & Software
segments.note: Automation software and control systems that run factories and process plants (includes AspenTech) — joint-fastest growing, helped by long-cycle project demand.

segments.name: Sensors
segments.note: Measurement instruments — sensors that track pressure, temperature and flow in industrial processes.

segments.name: Safety & Productivity
segments.note: Tools and safety products for industrial workers (such as Ridgid and Greenlee professional tools).

segments.name: Test & Measurement
segments.note: Electronic test and measurement equipment (the former NI business) — joint-fastest growing.

opex.name: SG&A expenses
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs — engineering, sales and running the company.

opex.name: Other deductions, net
opex.note: Mainly $203M of amortization of intangible assets from past acquisitions and $46M of restructuring costs, plus $25M of other items.

follow100Note: Segment rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Every business grew
takeaways.text: Net sales rose 7% to $5,201M, with all five businesses up: Control Systems & Software and Test & Measurement each grew 14%, Final Control 5%, Sensors 4% and Safety & Productivity 2%. Management said underlying orders rose 14% on exceptional long-cycle project activity. Full-year sales were $18,982M, up 5%.

takeaways.title: Profit grew much faster than sales
takeaways.text: Pre-tax earnings rose to $997M from $760M, and pre-tax margin widened to 19.2% from 15.6%. Adjusted segment EBITA — segment profit before interest, tax and amortization — was $1,511M at a 29.1% margin. Net earnings were $744M, or $1.33 a share, vs $609M and $1.07 a year ago (full-year EPS $4.79).

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS, and a higher dividend
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $1.86 vs $1.33 GAAP; the gap is mainly $203M of intangible amortization and $46M of restructuring in 'other deductions'. Emerson raised its quarterly dividend 7% to $0.595 a share and guided to fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of about $7.25, with about $2.5B of planned buybacks.

oneTimers: Other deductions, net of $274M include $203M of amortization of intangible assets and $46M of restructuring costs — the main items Emerson excludes to get from GAAP EPS of $1.33 to adjusted EPS of $1.86.
otherDetail: Other expense of $76M is interest expense, net.
footerNote: Operating income ($1,073M) is not a line Emerson reports; it is gross profit less SG&A and other deductions, net, before interest — pre-tax earnings of $997M plus net interest expense of $76M. Results are on a continuing-operations basis; there were no discontinued operations in the quarter, so net earnings equal earnings from continuing operations. Emerson had not yet filed its Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 when this report was prepared; all figures come from the official earnings release furnished with its Form 8-K on November 4, 2026.
